Professional

class Professional(id, name, type, institutionfacility)[source]

Bases: object

Represent a professional linked to an institution or facility.

Attributes:
idint

Unique identifier for the professional.

namestr

Full name of the professional.

typeint

Professional type code, a key of TYPE_MAP.

institutionfacilityInstitutionFacility

Institution or facility where the professional works. It may be None in an incomplete association, but then is_valid returns False.

TYPE_MAPdict[int, str], class attribute

Professional type codes (0 to 20) to pt_BR profession names; 0 is the empty “no type” entry.

PROPERTIESlist[str], class attribute

Field names, filled by initialize_reflexive.

DATA_PROPERTIESlist, class attribute

Field defaults, filled by initialize_reflexive.

Notes

The TYPE_MAP names are marked with QT_TRANSLATE_NOOP in the "Professional" context: this only registers the pt_BR source texts for pyside6-lupdate. They are translated at display time with QCoreApplication.translate in that context, so a language change takes effect immediately.

Serialization (get_data) stores the associated facility by its identifier.

Methods

get_data

Return the professional data as a one-item list.

Validate the professional object.

Update the fields from a dictionary.
is_valid()[source]

Validate the professional object.

Returns:
bool

True if the professional object is valid, False otherwise.

Notes

id must be an int, name must not be blank and type must be an int key of TYPE_MAP. institutionfacility must not be None.

Examples

>>> from types import SimpleNamespace
>>> facility = SimpleNamespace(id=3)
>>> hp = Professional(1, "Dr. Smith", 5, facility)
>>> hp.is_valid()
True
>>> Professional(1, "Dr. Smith", 5, None).is_valid()
False
>>> Professional(None, "", 99, facility).is_valid()
False
set_data(data)[source]

Update the fields from a dictionary.

Parameters:
datadict

Values keyed by field name. Keys that are not fields are ignored, and fields missing from data keep their value.

Notes

No validation or type conversion is done.

get_data()[source]

Return the professional data as a one-item list.

Returns:
list[dict]

A list with one dictionary of the field values, where institutionfacility is replaced by the facility id (None when there is no facility).

Examples

>>> from types import SimpleNamespace
>>> hp = Professional(1, "Dr. Smith", 5, SimpleNamespace(id=3))
>>> hp.get_data()[0]["institutionfacility"]
3
>>> Professional(1, "A", 5, None).get_data()[0]["name"]
'A'
